voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The British Museum, twenty twelve. Researchers lit a four-hundred-year-old map from beneath. John White drew it.
Under a small paper patch was a hidden fort symbol, drawn in bright red and blue.
White governed the Roanoke colony. In fifteen ninety, he found it deserted, with one word carved on a post: Croatoan.
He wrote that the settlers had planned to move fifty miles inland. The symbol sits where the Roanoke and Chowan rivers meet.
Digs near that spot have found a few English pottery sherds. Why it was covered is unknown. Where the colonists went has never been proved.
